title: How common is polymorphism? Every crystal in the Crystallography Open Database
question: How often does the same molecule crystallise in more than one solid form, and is that common among FDA-approved drugs?

headline.text: Of the 123 FDA-approved drugs crystallised at least twice in the open Crystallography Open Database, 72 (58%) show two or more distinct solid forms, vs 34% for organic compounds in general. A lower bound: the open database misses many known forms.

datasets.name: Crystallography Open Database (COD), bulk archive cod-cifs-mysql.zip
datasets.notes: Release of 2025-02-09 (SVN r297631), md5-verified. All CIFs parsed by our job array (108.9 GB uncompressed); COD's MySQL data table from the same archive used for duplicate/retraction flags and cross-checks. The live COD has grown since this release; we used the latest bulk archive.

datasets.name: FDA Orange Book (products.txt)
datasets.notes: Monthly data file (Oct 2026 edition); RX, OTC and discontinued products; ingredients split on ';'.

datasets.notes: Used only to get a structure (InChIKey) for each Orange Book ingredient.

compute.note: wall_minutes sums the elapsed time of every job / array task (not the critical path). 26813010 = first download attempt, cancelled after the COD server reset its 10 parallel connections (its finished byte ranges were reused by 26813661). 26816035 = 32-task parse array; with mit_normal congested, 8 tasks ran there and burst job 26816358 (mit_quicktest, 14 CPUs) parsed the other shards with the same script (3 shards were parsed by both at the same moment; outputs identical, written atomically), then the unstarted array tasks were cancelled. 26814637 = failed test run (bug fixed); 26816547 and 26816712 = superseded analysis runs; 26817191 = the run that produced this file.

method: Downloaded COD's single-file bulk archive (27.1 GB zip, 521,901 CIFs + MySQL dump) on mit_data_transfer; md5 verified. Chosen over the per-file rsync tree to avoid putting ~520k files on shared scratch.

Parsed every CIF straight from the zip with a 32-task job array (gemmi CIF parser, regex fallback): formula, names, space group, cell, Z, temperatures, pressures, COD id; COD's SQL table fills gaps and is used as a cross-check (agreement rates in stats.parse_qc).

Filtered out retracted / error-flagged, theoretical, duplicate and on-hold entries, entries with a recorded non-ambient pressure or a pressure study in the title, and non-integer (partial-occupancy) formulas; kept organic molecular crystals (C and H plus N, O, S, P, halogens, B, Si, Se only).

Same compound = same GCD-reduced Hill formula AND a shared normalised name (polymorph descriptors stripped); union-find within each formula. Cross-check: RDKit InChIKey connectivity block of COD's SMILES (single-component entries).

Same form = same space group (or a commonly mis-assigned or enantiomorphic pair such as Cc/C2/c or P3121/P3221) AND volume per non-H atom within 3% (+0.005% per K of temperature gap) after correcting to 293 K with the data-derived expansion coefficient (1.68e-4 /K); volume splits need recorded temperatures and are ignored at ~integer volume ratios (Z errors). Polymorphic = >= 2 forms, excluding cases whose only split is racemate vs enantiopure (one Sohncke, one non-Sohncke form).
FDA: Orange Book ingredients -> PubChem structure -> InChIKey of the active moiety; matched to neat COD entries by InChIKey connectivity (and by name + formula for entries without SMILES).
Validated on ritonavir, carbamazepine, paracetamol, sulfathiazole and ROY; sensitivity to tolerance, space-group-only rule and identity definition reported in stats.

findings: COD archive: 521,901 CIFs parsed by our job array; 447,032 pass the quality filters, of which 169,988 are organic molecular crystals.
Formula + name identity groups these into 166,537 compounds; 1,803 have >= 2 entries and 613 of those are polymorphic (34.0%, 95% CI 31.8-36.2%).
Volumetric thermal expansion estimated from 663 same-compound same-space-group pairs: median 1.68e-4 per K (IQR 1.23-2.13e-4).
Structure-key cross-check (InChIKey connectivity, single-component entries): 34.4% of 3,549 multiply-crystallised compounds are polymorphic.
Liberal upper bound (formula only, which merges isomers): 69.3% - shows why name or structure matching matters.

FDA Orange Book: 1,838 unique active moieties with a PubChem structure; 295 have a neat (single-component) crystal structure in COD; 123 have >= 2 entries and 72 of those show >= 2 forms (58.5%, 95% CI 49.7-66.9%).
361 FDA moieties also appear in COD as salts, solvates, hydrates or cocrystals - further solid forms not counted as polymorphs here.
paracetamol (acetaminophen): 21 neat COD entries by structure (2 forms), 30 by name (3 forms); literature: 3 (forms I-III at ambient pressure (paracetamol)).
carbamazepine: 16 neat COD entries by structure (3 forms), 0 by name (0 forms); literature: 5 (anhydrous forms I-V; Form V: Arlin et al., Chem. Commun. 47, 7074 (2011)).
ritonavir: 0 neat COD entries by structure (0 forms), 0 by name (0 forms); literature: 2 (Forms I and II; Bauer et al., Pharm. Res. 18, 859 (2001)).
sulfathiazole: 14 neat COD entries by structure (2 forms), 0 by name (0 forms); literature: 5 (forms I-V).
ROY: 4 neat COD entries by structure (1 forms), 9 by name (1 forms); literature: 10 (>= 10 forms; Yu, Acc. Chem. Res. 43, 1257 (2010); more reported since).
limitations: COD is open but incomplete: the CSD holds ~1.3M+ structures vs COD's ~0.5M, and most pharmaceutical polymorph data sit in the CSD or in company files. Counts here are lower bounds.
Most compounds were crystallised only once, so 'no second form seen' is not evidence of no polymorphism.
Solvates, hydrates and salts have different formulas and are deliberately NOT counted as polymorphs; a mis-entered formula (e.g. solvent omitted) can still create a false polymorph.

Name normalisation can fail both ways: different authors' systematic names for one compound do not merge (undercount), and an over-generic name could merge isomers (guarded by requiring the same formula).

Racemate vs enantiopure crystals of one constitution can look like two forms (flagged in stats as chirality_only); temperature-induced phase transitions count as distinct forms (flagged as forms not seen at similar temperatures).
Space-group mis-assignment and pseudo-symmetry (Z' > 1 superstructures) can split or merge forms.

The FDA comparison is confounded by attention: drugs are screened for polymorphs on purpose. The stratified chart compares compounds with the same number of determinations, which helps but does not remove that bias.

The Orange Book also lists amino acids, sugars and polyols (e.g. glycine, dextrose, mannitol) as active ingredients; they are included. Salts are matched through their largest organic component, so a metal salt maps to its organic ligand.

Repeat determinations of a compound are often published because something new (a new form) was found, which inflates polymorph shares among multiply-crystallised compounds; compare with deliberate screens: Stahly, Cryst. Growth Des. 7, 1007 (2007) reports roughly half of ~245 industrially screened compounds as polymorphic (published result).
This is about solid forms on Earth; it says nothing direct about microgravity crystallisation.
future_big_data: Repeat with the CSD (licensed, ~1.3M structures) and its curated polymorph and refcode-family fields.
Use full structure comparison (COMPACK / PXRD similarity) instead of cell volume to separate forms.
Join with FDA labels / DailyMed and patent data to find drugs whose approved form is metastable.
Mine the literature for polymorph screens and solid-form patents to estimate true form counts.

partners.name: CCDC (Cambridge Structural Database)
partners.why: Holds the most complete record of drug crystal forms; would turn these lower bounds into near-complete counts.
partners.evidence: COD (open) covers well under half of published organic structures; several famous forms are missing from COD (see famous_cases).

partners.name: Pharmaceutical solid-form teams (polymorph screening groups at drug makers and CROs)
partners.why: They decide which form is developed and would be the users of a form-controlled orbital process.
partners.evidence: Polymorphism is common among multiply-crystallised FDA active ingredients in this analysis.
